chunks: Had right been on their side they would have come to him submissively.
ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers refuse to accept the truth according to this verse?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often interpreted as a critique of the hypocrites (Munafiqun) whose rejection of the Prophet (peace be upon him) stems not from intellectual doubt but from the obstinacy of their ego (Nafs). It suggests that if the truth were undeniably theirs, their pride would compel them to submit, yet their attachment to worldly status keeps them in a state of willful blindness. This highlights the spiritual danger of letting self-interest override clear evidence, a key theme in understanding the psychological barriers to faith.
